items.title: Evolutionary Stability Does Not Guarantee Learning Accessibility: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Perspective on Cooperation Emergence
items.one_liner: Multi-agent reinforcement learning agents often fail to reach evolutionary stable cooperative outcomes due to differences between population-level stability and finite-sample learning dynamics.
items.summary: This research explores why evolutionary game theory's strategically stable outcomes do not always guarantee that finite-sample multi-agent reinforcement learning agents can reach cooperation through local rewards. Using a transparent three-agent governance game involving a government, a platform firm, and users inspired by the shared-bike setting, the authors compare evolutionary and learning basins. While the evolutionary basin covers the entire sampled grid with volume 1.00, empirical learning basins reach only 0.88 for epsilon-IQL and 0.00 for scaled Boltzmann and SA-EA BQL. Diagnostic traces reveal that action diversity and value separation can coexist with a failure to sustain cooperative joint action. These findings prove that evolutionary stability and learning accessibility remain fundamentally distinct properties in coupled game-learning systems.
items.bottom_line: Evolutionary stability does not guarantee learning accessibility in multi-agent reinforcement learning systems.

items.title: Just-in-Time Memory: Learning to Curate Task-Adaptive Memory for LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Just-in-Time Memory defers LLM agent memory curation to read time, drastically improving task adaptation and execution success rates.
items.summary: Researchers propose Just-in-Time Memory (JitMem), a read-time memory curation framework for LLM agents that avoids the limitations of write-time distillation. Traditional systems distill trajectories into fixed artifacts upon task completion, discarding contextual information before downstream queries are known. JitMem retains raw execution traces and synthesizes a task-adaptive payload at read time based on the active query, enabling the curator to be trained directly from immediate task success. Evaluations across ALFWorld, WebShop, and tau-bench show that JitMem significantly outperforms existing memory baselines.
items.bottom_line: Read-time memory curation overcomes the long-horizon credit-assignment bottlenecks inherent in write-time agentic memory models.

claims.text: JitMem consistently outperforms no-memory agents and memory methods, improving over the strongest baseline by 16.2, 16.3, and 3.9 absolute success-rate points.

items.title: Learning the Cost of Reliable Inference
items.one_liner: Dynamic auction routing platforms can expose 10% to 71% pricing margins in LLM inference, helping developers optimize procurement costs.
items.summary: Researchers have designed a procurement platform that uses a reverse second-price auction to route LLM queries based on provider competition and guaranteed quality levels rather than fixed token prices. By testing models from the Llama and Qwen families on mathematical reasoning and question-answering benchmarks, the authors found that pricing margins for the most cost-competitive provider vary between 10% and 71% depending on the task. This demonstrates substantial inefficiency in current fixed-price API markets and shows that dynamic auction routing can help users capture maximum savings. The findings suggest that token pricing should adapt dynamically to workload characteristics rather than relying on static pricing models.
items.bottom_line: Fixed-price LLM inference markets contain massive inefficiencies that can be exploited by dynamic auction platforms.
